text: Does a sech^2 soliton IC for v, with u perturbed from v^2/2 by +0.2v, survive as a single dominant peak with amplitude >= 1.0 (>=50% of 2.0) at T=8 in the coupled Burgers-swept-KdV system?

method: Fourier pseudospectral (rfft) spatial derivatives + explicit RK4 time stepping, no dealiasing, no hyperviscosity
bank_use_rationale: No bank available (NoKB). E1 is the simplest meaningful baseline: pseudospectral derivatives (required because v_xxx needs accurate high-k derivatives on periodic domain) paired with explicit RK4 (no IMEX, no operator splitting). dt=1e-4 satisfies CFL for dispersive term: |dt*k_max^3|=|1e-4*26.8^3|~1.93 < 2.83 (RK4 imaginary-axis stability limit).

diagnostics.mechanism: aliasing from nonlinear products (u*u_x, v*v_x, uv_x) folds high-k energy back into resolved modes

rationale: Blowup at t~0.65 due to aliasing instability. High-k energy in v grows exponentially before blowup. No dealiasing filter was applied; fix: add 2/3-rule dealiasing.

Aliasing from nonlinear terms causes blowup. Single-component upgrade: add 2/3-rule dealiasing to zero out modes |k| > Nx/3. Keep all else identical (same RK4, same dt, same pseudospectral derivatives).

method: Fourier pseudospectral + explicit RK4 + 2/3-rule dealiasing filter (zero modes |k|>Nx/3 after each nonlinear product)
bank_use_rationale: No bank. Single-component change from E1: add 2/3-rule dealiasing filter to suppress aliasing instability identified in F1 (high-k energy blowup at t~0.65). All other components identical.

diagnostics.soliton_tracking: moves from x=-5 at t=0 to x=-9.73 at t=8 (wraps periodically), speed decays from ~6 to ~1.8 consistent with amplitude loss
diagnostics.peak_vs_background: 2nd peak (11th grid pt) = 0.54, so structure is single dominant but broadened

rationale: Amplitude 0.635 < 1.0 threshold. Single dominant peak is present and mass is perfectly conserved (0%). Soliton motion is physically consistent (speed ∝ amplitude). Amplitude decay appears physical: soliton radiates energy due to ε=0.2 perturbation from Gardner reduction. E3 will try conservation-form nonlinear terms for cleaner dealiasing to rule out numerical amplitude dampening.

Single-component change: rewrite nonlinear terms in strict conservation form [u_t = -d/dx(3u^2/2 + 3v^2 + v_xx), v_t = -d/dx(3v^2+uv) - v_xxx]. This groups aliased products into a single spectral derivative rather than computing v*v_x and u*u_x separately, which can reduce spurious numerical dissipation from dealiasing. dt, Nx, IC unchanged.

method: Fourier pseudospectral + explicit RK4 + 2/3-rule dealiasing + CONSERVATION FORM: u_t = -d/dx(3u^2/2 + 3v^2 + v_xx), v_t = -d/dx(3v^2 + uv) - v_xxx
bank_use_rationale: No bank. Single-component change from E2: recast nonlinear flux terms in conservation form to compute a single dealiased spectral derivative of the flux, rather than dealiasing products of v*v_x and u*u_x separately. Eliminates potential spurious dissipation from component-wise dealiasing.

diagnostics.match_E2: bit-for-bit identical to E2 at all checkpoints

rationale: Conservation-form gives bit-identical results to E2, confirming (a) E2 dealiasing was correct and (b) amplitude decay is physical. Soliton structure survives as single dominant peak with mass perfectly conserved, but amplitude 0.635 < 1.0 threshold (50% of initial 2.0). Peak is 31.8% of initial due to radiation emission from ε=0.2 perturbation. All other criteria met: bounded (max|u|<15, max|v|<15), single dominant peak, mass drift=0%.
